claim: Under the ZeRO paper's mixed-precision accounting, model states cost 16 bytes per parameter (2 bytes bf16 weights + 2 bytes fp16 gradients + 12 bytes Adam optimizer state: 4 fp32 master copy, 4 momentum, 4 variance), so a 7B model needs more than 100 GB of VRAM before activations.
stance_target: the repo's claim that 7B fully trainable with Adam needs ~112 GB per card and therefore cannot fit DDP on 64 GB cards
scope_conditions: Mixed-precision Adam training; 7B parameters; excludes activations and temporary buffers
quoted_support: Optimizer states, such as those used in Adam, require an additional 12 bytes per parameter under the ZeRO paper's mixed-precision accounting (4 bytes for the fp32 master copy of the weights, 4 bytes for the momentum, and 4 bytes for the variance). Gradients in fp16 add another 2 bytes per parameter, putting the model states alone at 16 bytes per parameter. When combined with activations and temporary buffers, a 7B model can require more than 100 GB of VRAM.

claim: Plain DDP replicates parameters, gradients and optimizer state on every GPU, so at N GPUs it wastes (N-1)/N of aggregate memory on redundant copies; ZeRO-3 and FSDP shard those states to O(M/N) per GPU.
stance_target: the repo's claim that DDP's memory cost is per-card full-model state, which is what makes the frozen-Engram trick necessary
scope_conditions: DDP vs ZeRO-3/FSDP full-shard; N GPUs
quoted_support: Standard Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) is inefficient because it replicates these states across every GPU in the cluster. If you have 8 GPUs, you are essentially wasting 7/8ths of your total aggregate memory on redundant data. ... The memory footprint for model states on each GPU is reduced from O(M) to O(M/N), where M is the model size and N is the number of GPUs.

claim: Both ZeRO-3 and FSDP increase total communication volume by roughly 1.5x versus standard DDP, because they add an all-gather of parameters before each forward/backward and a reduce-scatter of gradients.
stance_target: the repo's claim that FSDP costs ~1.5x more communication than plain DDP on this fabric
scope_conditions: Full-shard ZeRO-3 / FSDP vs DDP; multi-node and single-node
quoted_support: Both ZeRO-3 and FSDP increase the total volume of data moved across the network by approximately 50% compared to standard DDP. Specifically, they require an all-gather operation to collect parameters before computation and a reduce-scatter operation to synchronize and shard gradients after computation.

claim: The 1.5x communication penalty makes sharded training highly sensitive to interconnect bandwidth: without a fast link the time spent waiting on all-gather/reduce-scatter can outweigh the benefit of larger effective batch sizes.
stance_target: the repo's claim that FSDP is the wrong choice on a 0.75 GiB/s all-reduce fabric
scope_conditions: ZeRO-3/FSDP on clusters without NVLink or high-speed inter-node networking
quoted_support: This makes the performance of these frameworks highly dependent on the interconnect bandwidth of the cluster. ... Without high-speed networking, the time spent waiting for data transfers can outweigh the benefits of larger batch sizes.

claim: CPU/NVMe offloading of optimizer state buys capacity at a 2x-10x throughput penalty because the PCIe bus becomes the bottleneck — the same PCIe bus that is already the bottleneck for collectives on this box.
stance_target: any plan that relies on ZeRO-Infinity-style offload to make a 7B model fit on this box
scope_conditions: DeepSpeed ZeRO-Offload / ZeRO-Infinity and FSDP cpu_offload
quoted_support: Yes, there is a significant performance penalty because the PCIe bus is much slower than GPU VRAM or NVLink. Training speed can drop by 2x to 10x depending on the model size and the amount of data being offloaded.

claim: FSDP2 (torch.distributed.fsdp.fully_shard) shards each parameter on dimension 0 as a DTensor and relaxes constraints around frozen parameters and sharded state dicts that save without extra communication — relevant if frozen Engram tables are to coexist with sharded training.
stance_target: whether frozen Engram tables can be carried inside an FSDP2 run rather than forcing plain DDP
scope_conditions: PyTorch FSDP2 API; frozen parameters; sharded state dicts
quoted_support: PyTorch documents the result as a more intuitive account of which slice of which tensor a rank owns, with relaxed constraints around frozen parameters and sharded state dicts that save without extra communication.

claim: This source is a vendor blog with no measurements of its own: its 16-bytes-per-param figure traces to the ZeRO paper (arXiv 1910.02054) and its 1.5x figure to the FSDP PVLDB paper, so the drafter should cite those primaries rather than this page.
stance_target: the evidence tier this source can carry
scope_conditions: Lyceum magazine article; sources section lists DeepSpeed ZeRO blog, HF Efficient Training on Multiple GPUs, and arXiv 2304.11277
